newsitem.title: USA: Apple sees sales rising in FY98-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Apple sees sales rising in FY98-analysts.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc executives told Wall Street analysts that the company could have double-digit revenue growth in fiscal 1998, analysts said Tuesday.

At a meeting with financial analysts in New York Monday, Fred Anderson, Apple's chief financial officer, said the company will continue to revamp its product lines and trim its expenses this year, analysts said.

"Fiscal 1997 will be a walk for them," said David Wu, a Chicago Corp analyst who attended the meeting. "Fiscal 98 will be the run." Wu and other analysts said Anderson did not give specific revenue and profit forecasts, but confirmed their revenue estimates.
Wall Street's revenue forecasts for the fiscal year ending September 1997 range from flat to an increase of five percent. Revenue could rise more than 10 percent in fiscal 1998, analysts said.

Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., reported more than $800 million in losses in the fiscal year ended September 27 amid declining sales of its Macintosh computers. In recent weeks, the company has released faster and cheaper computers and laptops to compete with offerings from companies such as Compaq Computer Corp and International Business Machines Corp.
In the most recent quarter, Apple reported an unexpected profit of $25 million, or 20 cents a share. Anderson said the company could have "sustainable profits" as early as the March quarter.
Apple's efforts to rebuild itself will take at least another year, analysts said.
"It's a three-year turnaround, and they just finished the first year," said Stephen Dube, analyst at Wasserstein Perella Securities.

On Tuesday, Apple's Anderson also told cable televisision channel CNBC that he expects Apple to maintain gross profit margins -- the percentage of money left over after costs of goods are subtracted from revenue -- of 20 percent or better, even though Apple is aggressively cutting prices on almost all of its products.
Anderson and other Apple executives could not immediately be reached for comment.
